business_problem: MishiPay needed to scale a self-scanning retail app that had to integrate 30 million inventory items, 7,500 promotion codes, real-time payments, and heterogeneous retailer data models without building complex custom infrastructure in-house.
solution_summary: MishiPay uses MongoDB Atlas as the core database service behind its self-scanning retail app, which links in-store inventory, pricing, promotions, payments, and reconciliation so shoppers can scan and buy items without queues. Atlas's multi-cloud document model lets the startup absorb heterogeneous retailer data and 30 million listed items without forcing each brand into one rigid schema, which is critical because every retailer exposes inventory and promotion data differently. The Atlas-backed platform processes real-time updates as transactions complete, pushing inventory adjustments and fund transfers while leaving room to expose the live database to retailer systems and third-party promotion APIs. With Atlas handling scale, resilience, and localized data needs, MishiPay can onboard customers faster, keep the service available around the clock, and use the resulting data foundation to build personalized in-store offers.

solution_components.name: MongoDB Atlas
solution_components.role: Stores product, promotion, transaction, and shopper data for MishiPay's self-scanning retail platform.

data_flow: Retailer inventory, pricing, and promotion data is stored in MongoDB Atlas, where the app reads product information for self-scan journeys and writes completed transactions back in real time. Atlas then supports inventory updates, fund transfers, reconciliation, and future promotion APIs tied to each shopper's behavior in store.
business_outcome: MongoDB Atlas keeps real-time inventory and transaction updates running for a 30-million-item, 14-country retail app, helping MishiPay reduce queue times, onboard retailers in two weeks, and support higher shopper frequency and spend.
